outputs: Model-generated answers (including refusals) to user queries

The models generate responses to user queries, and the study focuses on whether the model refuses to answer safe questions containing harmful words, aiming to reduce such false refusals through Self-Contrastive Decoding.

changes_made.explanation: Normalized model names to standard casing (LLaMA-2 instead of LlaMa2), removed duplicate model entries, simplified XSTest-Safe/Unsafe to XSTest, normalized wiki QA to WikiQA, and simplified the outputs description.

Removed 'Helpfulness' metrics since they are actually LLM-based evaluations (covered in Q3), not traditional automatic metrics. Normalized all perplexity variants to 'Perplexity' and refusal rate variants to 'Refusal Rate'.

methods: classification of responses into Compliance vs Refusal

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated similar evaluation methods into standardized names, normalized criteria names consistently.

guideline: Classify model responses as Compliance or Refusal to compute refusal rate, where Refusal includes full and partial refusal, and Compliance includes any direct attempt to answer
- Classify model responses as compliance or refusal to compute refusal rate.
Annotators classified each model response as Refusal or Compliance.

The prompt used for human evaluation is based on classifying responses as either Compliance or Refusal, where Refusal includes full or partial refusal, and Compliance includes any direct attempt to answer.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated multiple guideline descriptions into one comprehensive statement, normalized criteria to consistent format.

overall_notes: The paper addresses NLG evaluation by studying refusal behavior in LLMs when answering safe questions containing harmful words. It uses both automatic metrics (Perplexity, Refusal Rate) and LLM-based evaluation (GPT-4), plus human evaluation. The Self-Contrastive Decoding method is the main contribution. Extraction quality was good but needed normalization of model names and consolidation of duplicated/redundant items.
